HowItWorks.title: Book in minutes
HowItWorks.subtitle: Eight steps from choosing a car to handing back the keys. No online payment — we confirm the reservation with you before the car goes out.
HowItWorks.metaDescription: Renting from A&A Corporation step by step: pick a model, choose dates and a pick-up point, see the full price, confirm the booking, documents and handover.

steps.s1Desc: Browse the fleet, view the photos and the details. Availability depends on your dates, and we check it when you book.
steps.s2Desc: Set the dates, the times and one of the pick-up points available in the system. Collection is scheduled at least three hours ahead.
steps.s3Desc: The calculator uses the rates in force: the model, the length of the rental, the extras you pick and the pick-up point. You see the total and the deposit before you send anything.
steps.s4Desc: The driver details needed for the rental agreement. Nothing is paid online.
steps.s5Desc: You click the link we e-mail you. After you submit your reservation, we will confirm availability and terms. A request is an availability enquiry, not a concluded rental agreement.
steps.s6Desc: Once confirmed, we e-mail you the required rental documents — as attachments, so you have them to hand on any device.
steps.s7Desc: At the agreed place and time, on presentation of the driver's documents. We complete a handover report: the condition of the car, the odometer and the fuel level — raise anything you spot before you drive off.
steps.s8Desc: At the agreed place and time, with all the keys and equipment. We complete a report on return as well, and release the deposit where there are no grounds to hold it.

Partnership.lead: We are open to cooperation with private and business partners interested in expanding the A&A premium vehicle fleet. Below are the three forms we discuss most often.
Partnership.vehicleDesc: You contribute a specific car. A&A handles the rental, the customers, servicing and the day-to-day running of that car within the fleet.
Partnership.fleetDesc: You are interested in a share in developing a larger part of the fleet than a single car, with an agreed scope and horizon.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.intro: Revenue counts confirmed and completed bookings. Pending ones are not rentals yet. Expenses come from costs entered per vehicle. The purchase price is not a cost: it is the target the margin has to reach.

notice.noPrice: {count, plural, one {# unit has} other {# units have}} no purchase price entered, so {count, plural, one {it is} other {they are}} not counted in fleet recovery. Add it on the unit in the Fleet tab.

sections.costsIntro: Costs from the selected period, spread over days. An annual policy counts as 1/365 per day, not as one jump. You enter them on the car: Fleet → car → Expenses (one-off) and Recurring costs (leasing, insurance, parking).
sections.weekdaysIntro: Occupancy in the selected period, day by day of the week. This is the basis for weekend pricing.
sections.seasonIntro: Occupancy month by month. It becomes meaningful after a full year, when you can see whether February is weak or just was.
sections.mixNote: Customers are recognised by phone number from the customer file, not by surname. Two Smiths are two people, and one person can spell their surname three different ways.

economics.title: Unit profitability
economics.intro: Each car separately: what it earned, what it cost and how much of its purchase price it has already returned. Click a plate to see the day-by-day analysis. Free means days when the car was available and nobody booked it, which is a sales problem. Blocked means service and manual blocks, which is an operational problem. Fleet-wide: {freeDays, number} free and {blockedDays, number} blocked days, idle cost {idleCost}.

sales.title: Sales — month on month and year on year
sales.intro: Revenue for the last 12 months, each set against the same month a year earlier. The headlines count the last CLOSED month. The month in progress has only as many days as have passed, so compared with a full month it would always look like a collapse.
sales.noPrevYear: no data from a year earlier

monthly.title: Month by month
monthly.intro: The same 12 months in numbers. The chart shows the shape and the table verifies the values. It answers a question the daily chart cannot: was the last month weak, or is February always like this?

bookings.title: Bookings — how customers buy
bookings.intro: Last {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, {total, plural, one {# enquiry} other {# enquiries}}. ALL statuses count here. The point of this section is exactly how many enquiries did not turn into a rental.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.intro: Insurance and inspection: overdue, or expiring within 30 days.

documents.title: Inspection, insurance and service
documents.intro: Document and service status for each unit. You edit the dates on the unit in the Fleet tab. Five days before each one, a single reminder goes to {mailbox}.

car.since: Counted from {date}, {days} in the fleet. Revenue only from confirmed and completed bookings, spread over rental days. The purchase price is not a cost: it is the target the margin has to reach.

stat.netPositive: what the car earns each day it is owned
stat.netNegative: what the car loses each day it is owned

payback.title: Return on purchase
payback.noPrice: I cannot calculate the return without a purchase price. Enter it on the unit <link>in the Fleet tab</link>. Margin and utilisation are already calculated; only the target is missing.
payback.paidBack: The car has paid back its purchase price. Surplus:
payback.onPace: At the current pace ({perDay}) payback comes around
payback.overTwentySeven: At the current pace payback is more than 27 years away. That is arithmetic, not a forecast.
payback.never: At the current pace the car will not pay for itself: costs exceed revenue.

idle.title: Idle time and fixed cost
idle.share: {percent}% of the time the car is owned, it stands idle.
idle.explain: These are fixed costs multiplied by idle days: money spent on a car that earned nothing in that time. Zero means no fixed cost has been entered yet.

dep.title: Depreciation (loss of value)
dep.missing: I cannot calculate it without a book value and a period. Add them on the unit <link>in the Fleet tab</link>. It is usually the biggest cost of a car and never appears on an invoice. Without it the margin looks better than it is.
dep.explain: Depreciation is not part of the margin above. Margin means revenue minus the money actually spent. Here you see the full picture.

km.title: Cost and revenue per kilometre
km.missing: No odometer readings. Enter them on the rentals (pickup and return). This is the only measure that compares a cheap car with an expensive one fairly.
km.basis: Counted from {withKm} of {rentalsLabel}. Only those have both odometer readings.
km.lowData: With incomplete data the rate is overstated, because the full cost is divided by only part of the kilometres.

net.title: Cumulative result
net.intro: Revenue minus expenses, day by day, over the selected period. The dashed line is the purchase price. Where the curve crosses it is the day the car pays for itself.

day.title: Day by day
day.intro: In the {days}-day period: revenue {revenue}, expenses {expenses}. Hover over a bar to see a specific day.

funnel.title: Funnel — {period}
funnel.since: Counted from {since} — from that moment the system records these facts. Earlier conversations are left out, because for them “did not happen” and “we did not measure” look identical, and adding them together produced a funnel where more people clicked “Book” than ever saw the car.

steps.finishedHint: Counted from the source = chatbot field on the booking — from bookings actually created, not from clicks.

funnel.note: Each step is counted from its own real event: “Book” from a click in the chat, “started the form” from opening the booking page, “completed a booking” from the source field on the booking that was created. None is a copy of the previous step.

reasons.desc: Worked out from what happened, not guessed. “No data” is a full answer and appears whenever the traces do not point to one cause.
reasons.empty: No conversations without a booking in the selected period.
reasons.priceNote: There is deliberately no “price” entry here: nothing in the system tells apart a customer who saw the price and gave up from one who saw the price and went to compare. The number of people who saw a quote is in the funnel above — as a number, not as a reason.

questions.title: Unanswered questions
questions.subtitle: What customers searched for and the assistant could not answer — and what it answered although it was not sure. This is the list of things missing from the FAQ, and the cheapest source of knowledge about what the website lacks. Start with the “low confidence” items: there the customer left convinced they had got an answer.
questions.notice: “Add to FAQ” creates a draft with an empty answer. Nothing is generated automatically and nothing reaches the customer until you write the text and click “Approve and publish”. A published entry appears in two places at once — on the FAQ page and in the assistant — so that a second, invisible version of the rental terms is never created.
questions.counts: {rows, plural, one {# distinct question} other {# distinct questions}}, {total} occurrences in total

badges.lowConfidenceTitle: The assistant answered, but the match barely cleared the threshold. Check whether the answer was accurate.

questions.countersNote: “Got an answer” and “went to a person” are counted forward: when the assistant fails, it remembers the question and settles it on the next message in the same conversation. That is how you see the difference between a badly phrased question the customer managed around, and one they gave up on.

rules.title: Rental rules
rules.intro: One place used by the website, the FAQ, the chatbot and — eventually — voice support. A rule changed here works everywhere, without correcting the same information in several files.

documents.coreNote: Always in force, regardless of the switches below. It cannot be switched off — there is no rental without a driving licence and an identity document.
documents.explainer: Each switch answers the question “may we confirm this?”, not “is it so?”. Switching one off does not mean the opposite rule — the assistant simply stays silent on the subject and refers the customer to an A&A staff member.

mobywatel.title: We accept mObywatel
mobywatel.on: The assistant may tell customers that an identity document in the mObywatel app is accepted.
mobywatel.off: The assistant neither confirms nor rules out mObywatel acceptance — it refers the customer to an A&A staff member.

card.title: Payment card in the driver's name required
card.on: The assistant tells customers that a payment card in the driver's name is required.
card.off: The assistant does not claim that a card in the driver's name is mandatory. Company cases — company paying, employee driving — are decided by an A&A staff member.

nonEu.title: We accept non-EU driving licences
nonEu.on: The assistant informs about acceptance together with the conditions entered below.
nonEu.off: The assistant does not confirm acceptance of a non-EU licence on its own and refers the customer to A&A.
nonEu.notesPlaceholder: Empty — to be filled in by the owner
nonEu.notesOn: This text will be added to the assistant's answers and to the FAQ.
nonEu.notesOff: Saved but not used while the switch is off.

age.explainer: The switches in this section answer the question “does this requirement apply?” — unlike the documents section, where they answer “may we confirm this?”. That is why they are labelled APPLIES / DOES NOT APPLY here.
age.offNote: Switching off a class requirement does not remove the age check — it reduces it to the safety threshold of {min} years, which always applies and cannot be switched off from the panel.
age.enforcedOn: The booking form enforces class thresholds — it checks the driver's age against the class of the chosen car.
age.enforcedOff: The booking form rejects drivers under {min}, as before. Class thresholds are saved, but not yet in effect.
age.oneSource: One source for everyone: the form, backend, FAQ, offer pages and the assistant read the same value. A customer will never see a threshold the form does not apply.
age.legalBody: The Terms (§3, PL and EN) say: at least {min} years old and a driving licence issued at least a year earlier, and for selected models they allow a higher age stated when the booking is confirmed. The 25-year threshold fits within that wording, but the form rejects earlier — at the moment the booking is made. To be settled with a lawyer before enforcement is switched on; the full list of places is in docs/ZLECENIE-WIEK-KIEROWCY.md. The panel does not change the legal document.

requirement.onEnforced: Applies: {years} years. The form, FAQ, offer pages and the assistant all state the same number.
requirement.onStored: Saved as {years} years, but not in effect today: enforcement of class thresholds is off, so {min} years applies. Nobody will see this number until you switch on the toggle below.
requirement.off: This class falls back to the safety threshold: {min} years. Switching it off does not remove the age check — it lowers it to {min}.

licence.note: The booking form does not collect the date a driving licence was issued, so the system cannot be asked to check tenure. Until that field is added, tenure is off everywhere: it does not block bookings and does not appear in the FAQ, on offer pages or in the assistant's answers.
licence.locked: A separate task — together with confirming the requirements with the insurer.

enforce.label: Enforce class thresholds in the booking form
enforce.on: The form checks the age against the class of the chosen car and rejects bookings below the threshold. A car without a class gets {min} years.
enforce.off: One threshold applies to the whole fleet: {min} years — exactly how the form has worked so far. Class thresholds are saved, but not in effect and nobody sees them.
enforce.floorNote: The age check cannot be switched off. {min} years is a threshold written into the code as a safeguard and applies regardless of settings — also when the configuration cannot be read or a car has no class.
enforce.blocked: Blocked: {count} published cars have no class. Assign them in the table below, then the switch becomes available.

notes.audit: Every change is recorded in the Event log, together with what was there before and who made it.
notes.faq: An active rule appears in the FAQ and with the assistant, from the same text. A rule that “needs a decision” appears nowhere — the assistant refers the customer to a staff member instead.

googleMaps.placeIdHint: The technical identifier of the location on Google. Customers never see it. You will find it in the business profile or with Google’s “Place ID Finder” tool. It must belong exactly to A&A — the ID of a similarly named business would link our site to someone else’s address.
googleMaps.coordsHint: The map pin coordinates. In Google Maps: right-click the pickup point — the first item in the menu is these two numbers. They go onto the map on the contact page and into the structured data. Customers do not see them as numbers.
googleMaps.reviewsHint: Copy exactly what the business profile shows. The site cannot fetch these numbers by itself, and that is not an oversight: the Google Places API requires a project with billing enabled, and scraping search results is expressly prohibited by its terms. The project rule is “no new costs”, so there is one honest way out — these two fields.
googleMaps.reviewsEmpty: Empty fields are not an error. The bar then shows only the “Read all reviews” link, without stars and without a rating. Leave them empty until the profile has reviews — a five entered “to encourage people” would be a lie that a customer can check in one click.
googleMaps.showHeading: What to show on the site
googleMaps.enabledButMissing: Switched on, but {missing} — nothing will show on the site. This is deliberate: we do not show customers a button that leads nowhere.

map.label: Show map
map.hint: A map with a pin on the contact page. Needs no API key or Google account — costs nothing.
map.missing: the coordinates (lat and lng) are incomplete

googleButton.label: See us on Google
googleButton.hint: Opens the business profile on Google. Customers see the same label on the contact page.
googleButton.missing: the “Google Business profile link” field is empty

reviewButton.label: Add a review
reviewButton.hint: Sends the customer straight to the review form. Customers see the same label on the contact page.

reviewBar.label: Review bar
reviewBar.hint: One line above the map: stars, rating, number of reviews and “Read all reviews”. The link goes to the reviews of THIS profile — unlike “Add a review”, which opens the form for a new one.
reviewBar.missing: there is neither a Place ID nor a profile link

googlePage.title: GOOGLE
googlePage.subtitle: Google Business profile, map, reviews and location. Each item has its own switch — a switch that is on without data will not show to customers.
googlePage.emptyNote: Empty fields are not an error. The links, Place ID and coordinates come from the business’s Google profile — until it is set up and verified there is nothing to enter here, and the public site simply does not show these items. Nothing needs to be set “just in case”.

actions.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
actions.socialUrl: Every link must start with http:// or https://

upload.tooLarge: The file is too large — 8 MB at most.
upload.unsupportedType: Unsupported format. Allowed: JPG, PNG, WEBP.
upload.writeFailed: The file could not be saved.

actions.emptySlot: There is no photo in this slot.
actions.nowOnSite: Photo {n} is now on the site.
actions.removedDark: Photo removed — the dark theme goes back to the default.
actions.removedLight: Photo removed — the light theme has no photo.
actions.companyInvalid: Check the details — the email address must be valid, the map link must start with http:// or https://, and the hours must be in HH:MM format.
actions.chatbotEmailInvalid: Check the email address for handing over conversations.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: The state read from the running systems. Nothing here is typed in by hand — if something shows green, it reported in by itself.

systems.heading: Systems
systems.stale: should report every {interval} and has gone silent
systems.unknownNote: “Unknown” means that check has never reported. The scripts save their state on every run, so the first entries appear after the next run — monitoring every 15 minutes, backup at 03:00 at night.

cache.intro: The image build cache grows with every deployment and does not clean up after itself — in August it grew to 14 GB and pushed disk usage to 83%. The server checks it every 15 minutes and cleans up on its own only once disk usage reaches {threshold}%. Below the threshold it deletes nothing and only records the measurement.
cache.scope: Only the build cache is cleaned. Production images, rollback images, containers, volumes (database, media, certificates), backups and snapshots are outside the reach of this mechanism — even when the disk is full. If usage still exceeds {alert}% after cleaning, the server sends an alert and waits for a human decision instead of deleting anything more.
cache.statusFail: Disk full despite cleaning — a decision is needed

logins.heading: Panel sign-ins
logins.intro: Straight from the event log — the same one someone investigating a break-in would look at.
logins.lockout: . The account locks itself after a run of failed attempts, and an address that tries too fast is refused for five minutes.

accounts.heading: Accounts
accounts.summary: {total, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}}, {active} active, {superadmins} with full permissions{locked, plural, =0 {} other {, # locked}}.
accounts.singleAccount: One account is one point of failure. A lost password or a locked account means no access to the panel until it is recovered by hand from the server.
accounts.noTwoFactor: Two-factor sign-in (2FA): not active on any account. The mechanism is ready — it is switched on under Settings → My account, together with ten backup codes. Without 2FA, the only barrier between a stranger and the panel is the password.
accounts.withTwoFactor: Two-factor sign-in (2FA): active on {count, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}}.

protection.heading: Bot protection
protection.missingVars: The TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY variables are missing. The keys are created in the Cloudflare dashboard (Turnstile → Add site), they are free, and enabling them only needs a container restart — no image rebuild. Until then the forms are guarded by a honeypot trap, a fill-time check and rate limits, which work ALWAYS and do not depend on any external service.
protection.none: Nothing has been rejected. That is a normal result for a small site — an empty log does not mean the protection is not working.
protection.logNote: The log records the time, the type of block, the route and a SHORTENED identifier — not the IP address and not the email. Entries can only be appended: they cannot be changed or deleted from the panel.

recovery.heading: Recovery
recovery.intro: Actions run from the server console — the panel does not run them on purpose. A “restore database” button in the browser is one click away from deleting a day’s work.

buildCache.confirm: Are you sure you want to delete the unused Docker build cache?
buildCache.confirmNote: Production images, rollbacks, volumes and backups will not be deleted.
buildCache.awaiting: A cleanup is already queued — the server will run it within a minute.
buildCache.footer: The button only queues docker builder prune. The panel has no access to Docker — the request is picked up by a script on the server, and that script cannot remove anything but the build cache.

cacheActions.alreadyQueued: A cleanup has already been queued or is running right now. Refresh the page in a moment.
cacheActions.queued: Build cache cleanup queued. The server will run it within a minute — refresh the page.
cacheActions.failed: The cleanup could not be queued.

chatbot.title: Assistant (chatbot)
chatbot.subtitle: Automatic handling of questions when nobody is at the phone.

master.label: Assistant enabled
master.hint: When switched off, nothing appears on the site — regardless of the other settings.

basics.heading: Basics
basics.name: Assistant name
basics.modeHybrid: Hybrid — rules + model for hard questions
basics.modeHint: The deterministic mode answers from your data: the price list, the fleet, availability and the FAQ. It uses no external model, needs no API key and generates no monthly costs. It cannot understand an arbitrarily phrased sentence, though — when unsure, it asks a follow-up question or suggests contacting a person.
basics.autoOpenHint: “Automatic opening” is off by default. A pop-up right after arrival is one of the most irritating things on a rental site, and whoever needs help will click it themselves.
basics.hoursNote: “Only outside opening hours” takes its schedule from Company and contact details — one source of truth about when you are available. When someone is at the phone, the bot does not compete with a human.

ai.killHint: All traffic goes back to the rules from the next message. No restart, no deployment. The chatbot keeps working.
ai.capNote: The {cap} neuron limit is 80% of the free Cloudflare allowance. Once it is used up, the model is no longer asked and the assistant answers with the rules — with no error visible to the customer and no possibility of a charge. The counter resets at midnight UTC.

can.heading: What the assistant may do
can.intro: In the worst case, each of these things ends with a badly phrased sentence — never with a wrong transaction.
can.faqHint: Deposit, documents, mileage limit, driver age
can.offerHint: Which cars are in the fleet and how they differ
can.availabilityHint: Which cars are free on the given dates
can.pricesHint: From the price list, taking the rental length into account — no discounts
can.startBookingHint: Collects the date and car, passes them to the form. Does not confirm
can.handoffLabel: Hand the conversation over to a person
can.handoffHint: When it does not know, or the customer asks for a person

limits.heading: What the assistant will never do
limits.intro: Deliberately without switches. These are not preferences, just limits written into the bot’s code — a checkbox “the bot may refund money” is a checkbox someone will one day tick.

handover.heading: Handover and texts
handover.email: Email for handing over conversations (empty = company address)
handover.greetingPlaceholder: Hello, how can I help you?
handover.fallbackPlaceholder: I will pass this on to our team — we will get back to you in the morning.

account.title: My account
account.loadFailed: The account could not be loaded. Please sign in again.

password.heading: Password
password.note: Changing the password also resets the failed-attempt counter, so it unlocks an account that was locked after a run of wrong sign-ins.

login.heading: Sign-in
login.recoveryNote: A lost phone TOGETHER with the backup codes sheet is the only situation in which 2FA has to be removed from the server console: npx tsx scripts/wylacz-2fa.ts. Whoever has a shell on the server already has the database and the secrets — this route opens nothing new, and it saves you from being locked out of your own panel.
login.history: Full history of your actions: <link>Event log</link>.

profile.name: Full name
profile.emailNote: The email address is the login — it is changed in account management, not here. This is deliberate: if it could be changed from an open session, a hijacked session would mean a hijacked account.

twoFactor.heading: Two-factor sign-in (2FA)

setup.intro: Open an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Aegis, 1Password, Authy), add the account manually by entering the key below. Then type the six digits the app shows.
setup.otpauth: otpauth:// address (for apps that accept it)

disable.note: Turning it off requires the password AND a current code — two factors to remove two factors. The backup codes will be deleted.

codes.title: Backup codes — save them NOW
codes.intro: This is the only time you will see them. The database holds only hashes — nobody, including us, can read them later. Each code works once and is entered instead of the app code when you do not have your phone.
codes.savedCheck: I have saved the codes somewhere safe, off this computer.

twoFactor.enabledNow: 2FA is on. At the next sign-in the panel will ask for an app code.

sessions.heading: Sign out of all devices
sessions.note: Invalidates EVERY open session of this account — including this one. Use it when you left the panel signed in on someone else’s computer or suspect that someone knows your password.

start.alreadyOn: 2FA is already on for this account.

confirm.expired: The setup has expired (10 minutes). Start again — the previous QR code is no longer valid.
confirm.wrongCode: The code does not match. Check that the same email address appears in the app and that your phone’s clock is set automatically.

reissue.reissued: New codes issued. The previous ones no longer work.

sessions.revoked: All sessions invalidated. You will shortly be taken to the sign-in screen — in this tab too.

legal.title: Legal documents
legal.intro: The saved version replaces the built-in text and is published at {path}. The content is filtered for security when saved.

status.custom: The custom version (edited in the panel) is published.

legalEditor.linkInvalid: The link must start with http://, https://, mailto: or tel:
legalEditor.heading: Section heading
legalEditor.builtInNote: The built-in document text is shown. The first save creates a custom version, which will be published from then on.

twoFactorEnrol.enabledIntro: This account is protected by a second factor. If you have your recovery codes in front of you, save them now — this is the only time they are readable.
twoFactorEnrol.enableIntro: The A&A panel requires a second factor at sign-in. Without it, the only barrier between a stranger and the bookings, pricing and customer data is a password — and passwords leak from services where nobody has changed them for years.
twoFactorEnrol.enabledHow: You can issue new recovery codes at any time under Settings → My account. Issuing a new set invalidates the previous one.
twoFactorEnrol.enableHow: This takes two minutes: an authenticator app on your phone, one code to confirm, and ten recovery codes to store somewhere safe. Recovery codes are your way back in if you lose your phone.
twoFactorEnrol.footer: Signed in as {email}. If you do not have your phone with you right now, 2FA can be removed from the server console: npx tsx scripts/wylacz-2fa.ts — but until then the panel stays locked.

users.title: Users
users.intro: Accounts with access to the admin panel. There is no public sign-up; accounts are created here only.
users.ownPasswordSubtitle: Change the password of your own account. The current password is required.
users.newUserSubtitle: The new account can sign in straight away
users.accountsSubtitle: Edit details, role and password, deactivate or delete accounts
users.rolesNote: The Superadmin role gives access to this page and account management. The Administrator role gives full access to the rest of the panel, but not to accounts.
users.cannotManage: Adding, editing and deleting accounts requires the Superadmin role.
users.passwordVisibleNote: The password is shown so it can be written down and passed to the new user. Afterwards it cannot be read again, only replaced.
users.selfNote: Your own role and active status cannot be changed. This protects you from locking yourself out.
users.inactiveNote: An inactive account cannot sign in and loses access immediately, but its history stays in the activity log.
users.setPasswordNote: Sets a new password for {email} and lifts any lock. Share it over a secure channel.
users.deleteConfirm: Delete the account {email} permanently? Activity log entries will remain, but will no longer be linked to the account.
users.genericError: Something went wrong. Please try again.
users.passwordMin: Password must be at least {min} characters long.
users.cannotDemoteSelf: You cannot remove your own permissions.
users.cannotDeactivateSelf: You cannot deactivate your own account.
users.lastSuperadmin: This is the last active Superadmin. At least one must remain.
users.duplicateEmail: An account with this e-mail address already exists.
users.passwordsDiffer: The new passwords do not match.
users.cannotDeleteSelf: You cannot delete your own account.
users.lastSuperadminDelete: This is the last active Superadmin and cannot be deleted.
